plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU) to zero for capital preservation.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Increase QQQI to 36% to favor income and broad index exposure.
This plan aims for a steady, low-drawdown portfolio.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a potential ~1.5% monthly return, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration, but also limits upside potential.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU) to small allocations.
Reduce SPY to 20% to meet the single name mandate.
Buy MRVL at 4% as a strong scanner setup to blend quality tech.
This plan balances broad index, quality tech, and a little leverage.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets a potential ~2.5% monthly return, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while maintaining exposure to quality tech and broad market indices.

plan: Increase leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU) to lean into growth.
Trim SPY to 20% to meet the single name mandate.
Buy MRVL at 6% as a high-scoring scanner setup.
This plan uses leverage and concentrates in strong setups for stretch growth.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets a potential ~4% monthly return, aiming for stretch growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups, which raises both upside and drawdown potential. Be aware of daily decay and rebalancing in leveraged ETFs, and maintain strict stop discipline as losses can accumulate rapidly.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU) to zero.
Trim high-beta single names CRWD to 5% and SNOW to 1%.
Add QQQI to 50% to prioritize steady monthly distributions.
This plan focuses on low drawdown and reliable income over growth.
income.read: This income plan targets a potential ~1% monthly return, prioritizing steady distributions. It significantly reduces exposure to high-beta and leveraged assets. While aiming for reliable income, distributions are variable and NAV can still decline in market downturns; this is not a savings account.
